name: Orzo al Limone with Crispy Parmesan Chicken
desc: Creamy lemon Parmesan orzo topped with thin panko and Parmesan crusted chicken cutlets.

source.title: Orzo al Limone with Crispy Parmesan Chicken
source.evidence: Saved Instagram reel; caption and on-screen text captured in the owner's saved-recipes export

ingredients.raw: 1 lb boneless skinless chicken breasts, halved horizontally into 4 thin cutlets
2 tbsp olive oil, plus more as needed
1 tbsp olive oil, plus more for drizzling
2 cups chicken broth, plus more as needed
1 large lemon, zested and juiced, plus more for serving
ingredients.prep: zested and juiced, plus more for serving

ingredients.raw: 1/4 cup finely grated Parmesan, plus more for serving

steps: Set up three shallow bowls: the flour mixed with 1/2 tsp of the kosher salt and the black pepper; the beaten eggs; and the panko mixed with the Parmesan and garlic powder.
Cover each cutlet with parchment and pound it to an even 1/4 in thickness with a meat mallet or heavy pan.
Dredge each cutlet in the flour, then the egg, then the panko mixture, pressing the crumbs on firmly.

Heat the olive oil in a large saute pan over medium-high heat until shimmering. Fry the cutlets in a single layer, in batches, about 4 min per side until deeply golden and cooked through (165°F). Add more oil between batches if the pan looks dry.
Move the chicken to a wire rack, sprinkle with flaky salt while hot, and rest a few minutes. Slice into strips if you like.
For the orzo, heat the olive oil and butter in a large high-sided saute pan over medium heat. Cook the shallot and garlic 1 min, stir in the black pepper, and cook 1 min more.

Stir in the orzo and toast 2 min. Add the broth, bring to a boil, then simmer 10-15 min, stirring often, until the orzo is tender and most of the liquid is absorbed. Add a splash more broth or water if it thickens before the orzo is done.
Off the heat, stir in the lemon zest and juice, Parmesan, cream and the remaining 1/4 tsp kosher salt until creamy. Taste and add more lemon if you like.
Divide the orzo among bowls and top with the chicken, more Parmesan, cracked pepper, lemon zest and juice, and a drizzle of olive oil.
tips: Grate the Parmesan fresh so it melts smoothly. Toasting the orzo adds flavor.
Orzo keeps absorbing liquid, so loosen leftovers with warm broth. Half-and-half or milk can replace the cream.
Crisp leftover chicken in the oven or air fryer.
